stories.headline: Canada hits back with tariffs up to 50% on $20bn of US goods after trade talks collapse

key_facts.fact: Canada announced on Tuesday, Aug. 25, counter-tariffs on C$27.6bn (about $19.9bn) of US goods, matching 'dollar for dollar' the 50% duties Trump imposed on Canadian imports over the weekend.
key_facts.excerpt: On Tuesday, the Canadian government said it would impose tariffs on 27.6 billion Canadian dollars, or $19.9bn, worth of US goods, matching 'dollar for dollar' the new US duties that Trump imposed.

key_facts.fact: The counter-tariffs cover more than 700 US products at rates from 15% to 50% and take effect on September 8, targeting steel and aluminium, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, plastics and electronics.
key_facts.excerpt: The counter-tariffs will impact more than 700 products, the government said in a statement... The tariffs will range from 15 percent to 50 percent and take effect on September 8.

key_facts.fact: Ottawa doubled its counter-tariff on US steel and aluminium products from 25% to 50%, and added a C$7.5bn ($5.42bn) support package for businesses and workers hit by the trade war.
key_facts.excerpt: A 50% tariff on steel and aluminum products that were previously only subject to a 25% counter tariff... Canada will also offer businesses and workers impacted by US tariffs an additional C$7.5bn for support programmes.

key_facts.fact: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said the US terms were 'uneconomic, unfair, and ultimately unacceptable' and that Washington 'asked too much of Canada and offered too little in return'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Ultimately, the terms proposed by the U.S. administration were uneconomic, unfair, and ultimately unacceptable," Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Trump on Tuesday called Canada 'easily the most difficult and unreasonable' country he deals with and floated renaming Lake Ontario 'Lake America'; he had said Monday that US tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks and parts would rise to 50% on Jan. 1.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump lashed out at Canada on Tuesday morning, suggesting on Truth Social that the U.S. would halt business with Ontario, and repeatedly floating the prospect of renaming Lake Ontario to 'Lake America.'

key_facts.fact: Bilateral US-Canada trade was worth around $872.3bn in 2025, and the escalation puts the future of the USMCA free trade pact in question.
key_facts.excerpt: Canada is one of the United States' largest trading partners, accounting for around $872.3 billion in bilateral trade in 2025.

stories.headline: Oil sinks below $90 as Washington sends diplomats back to Middle East embassies

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell 3.6% on Tuesday, Aug. 25, to $87.27 a barrel — a second straight decline after 13 gains in 14 sessions — while WTI dropped more than 3% to a one-week low.
key_facts.excerpt: the price for a barrel of Brent crude fell 3.6% to $87.27 for a second decline following 13 gains in 14 days.

key_facts.fact: The slide followed a New York Times report that the US State Department is preparing to send diplomats back to Middle East embassies evacuated before and during the war with Iran, signalling Washington does not expect a return to all-out hostilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Crude prices tumbled on Tuesday on a news report that the US would be returning diplomats to Middle East embassies, easing concerns about an escalation of the Iran war.

key_facts.fact: The drop came despite the US announcing new sanctions on Iran and its trading partners on Monday under 'Operation Economic Outcast'; AJ Bell's Dan Coatsworth said the sanctions were 'less severe than anticipated'.
key_facts.excerpt: "US sanctions on Iran were less severe than anticipated," said Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, adding that lower oil prices helped markets to regain some poise as government bond yields eased back from their recent highs.

key_facts.fact: Falling crude eased inflation expectations: the 10-year Treasury yield dropped about 6 basis points to 4.637% on Tuesday, from 4.74% at the end of the prior week, after touching multi-year highs.
key_facts.excerpt: WTI crude oil fell more than -3% on Tuesday, easing inflation expectations and knocking the 10-year T-note yield down by -6 bp to 4.64%.

key_facts.fact: US equities closed higher on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 up 0.3% to 7,677.28, the Dow up 160.24 to 53,577.40 and the Nasdaq up 0.7% to 26,151.30.
key_facts.excerpt: All told, the S&P 500 rose 24.42 points to 7,677.28. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 160.24 to 53,577.40, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 171.11 to 26,151.30.

key_facts.fact: Oil fell again early Wednesday, Aug. 26, with Brent down 2.52% to $86.35, on the prospect of an Iran-Oman deal to secure safe transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: International benchmark Brent crude futures for October delivery declined 2.52% to $86.35 a barrel... crude oil futures fell more than 2% on the potential for a deal between Iran and Oman to secure a safe transit route through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: US inflation stays hot: July PCE at 3.7%, above forecasts, with core steady at 3.3%

key_facts.fact: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis reported on Wednesday, Aug. 26, that the July PCE price index rose 0.2% on the month and 3.7% year over year — both 0.1 percentage point above the Dow Jones consensus.
key_facts.excerpt: The personal consumption expenditures price index... increased a seasonally adjusted 0.2% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.7%, the Commerce Department reported Wednesday. Both were 0.1 percentage point above the Dow Jones consensus.

key_facts.fact: Core PCE, which strips out food and energy and is the Fed's preferred trend gauge, rose 0.2% on the month and 3.3% year over year, in line with forecasts and unchanged from June.
key_facts.excerpt: But stripping out volatile food and energy costs, core PCE posted respective gains of 0.2% and 3.3%, in line with forecasts.

key_facts.fact: Services inflation accelerated to 0.3% from 0.1% in June while goods prices fell 0.1%; headline PCE has now been at 3.7% for two straight months, against a Fed target of 2%.
key_facts.excerpt: Services inflation accelerated to 0.3% from 0.1% in the previous month, while goods prices fell 0.1% (vs -0.6%)... On an annual basis, headline PCE inflation remained unchanged at 3.7%, above expectations of 3.6%.

key_facts.fact: Personal income rose 0.4% in July and consumer spending rose 0.2%, with real personal spending flat on the month.
key_facts.excerpt: Personal income increased 0.4% and consumer spending rose 0.2% in July.

key_facts.fact: Markets are pricing a 39% chance of a 25 basis-point Fed rate hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting; Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Tuesday it would be appropriate to tighten 'soon' absent sustained inflation progress.
key_facts.excerpt: The markets are discounting a 39% chance of a +25 bp rate hike at the next FOMC meeting on September 15-16... "Maintaining the current federal funds rate target range will require continued evidence that inflation is indeed coming down..."

key_facts.fact: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is due to speak Friday at the Kansas City Fed's Jackson Hole symposium, his first major venue since the reading.
key_facts.excerpt: Investors are also eyeing Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's speech on Friday at the Fed's annual symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming.

stories.headline: Zelensky awards Musk Ukraine's Order of Freedom as Kyiv presses for Starlink over Russia

key_facts.fact: A presidential decree published Wednesday, Aug. 26, awarded Elon Musk the Order of Freedom, Ukraine's highest honour for foreign nationals, citing his 'outstanding personal merits' in protecting human life and freedom and developing Ukraine-US relations.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Wednesday awarded Elon Musk the Order of Freedom, one of Ukraine's highest state honors, for his 'outstanding personal merits' in protecting human life and freedom and strengthening ties between Ukraine and the United States.

key_facts.fact: The decree names Musk as 'entrepreneur, engineer, chief executive of SpaceX and Tesla, United States' and makes no reference to Starlink or the ongoing military negotiations.
key_facts.excerpt: "The Order of Freedom is awarded to Elon Musk - entrepreneur, engineer, chief executive of SpaceX and Tesla, United States," the decree states.

key_facts.fact: Kyiv wants Starlink connectivity for unmanned systems operating up to roughly 200km inside Russia, to hunt mobile ballistic-missile launchers such as Iskanders before they fire.
key_facts.excerpt: Kyiv wants the ability to use Starlink-connected unmanned systems against mobile launchers operating as far as approximately 200km inside Russia.

key_facts.fact: Musk currently permits Starlink use inside Ukrainian territory, including Russian-occupied regions, but restricts it over Russia itself, arguing wider use would be an escalation; Zelensky said on Aug. 22 that Musk 'may change his mind once he sees further arguments'.
key_facts.excerpt: "So far, (Elon Musk) has said that this constitutes an escalation," Zelensky said. "However, he may change his mind once he sees further arguments."

key_facts.fact: SpaceX cut off Russian forces' use of Starlink terminals in occupied territory in February 2026, a move Zelensky credits with contributing to Ukraine's 2026 battlefield gains in 'middle-strike' drone operations 50-200km from the front line.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's decision earlier this year to accept Kyiv's pleas and block unauthorized Starlink terminals being used by Russian forces in occupied territory also strengthened Ukraine's position.

stories.headline: France lifts SCALP licence restrictions, clearing Ukraine to build Storm Shadow missiles at home

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said on Aug. 25, at a press conference in Kyiv with Estonian President Alar Karis, that Ukraine has received approval from the UK and France to produce long-range Storm Shadow/SCALP cruise missiles domestically.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine has received approval from the U.K. and France to produce long-range Storm Shadow/SCALP missiles, President Volodymyr Zelensky said during a press conference with Estonian President Alar Karis in Kyiv on Aug. 25.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said Macron confirmed that restrictions on the SCALP missiles and the related licences would be lifted: 'We had previously spoken with President Macron, and he confirmed that the SCALPs and the license had been unlocked.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We received confirmation from the United Kingdom regarding the production of long-range SCALP missiles. We had previously spoken with President Macron, and he confirmed that the SCALPs and the license had been unlocked," the president said.

key_facts.fact: The SCALP/Storm Shadow is a French-British cruise missile with a range of up to 250km (155 miles), designed for precision strikes on fixed targets at night and in poor weather.
key_facts.excerpt: The SCALP is a long-range cruise missile built jointly by France and the U.K., which calls it the Storm Shadow. It has a range of up to 250 kilometers (155 miles).

key_facts.fact: Zelensky also said Ukraine expects a roadmap within 7-10 days for the Freyja anti-ballistic missile project, and confirmed incoming deliveries of Crotale air-defence systems with VT-1 missiles, AIM missiles and additional Patriot interceptors.
key_facts.excerpt: The president also announced that within 7–10 days, Ukraine will have a roadmap for cooperation on the FREYJA anti-ballistic missile system... several Crotale air defense systems and missiles for them; AIM missiles used by air defenses to intercept Russian missiles.

key_facts.fact: Separately on Aug. 25, Ukrainian and Finnish companies signed documents at a Kyiv roundtable chaired by Zelensky and Finnish President Alexander Stubb covering drone production in Finland for Ukraine and Europe, unmanned maritime systems, and a plant for unmanned ground vehicles.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian and Finnish companies signed documents on the implementation of joint defence projects. These concern the development and production of drones in Finland for the needs of Ukraine and Europe, the development of capabilities in unmanned maritime systems, and the establishment of a facility producing unmanned ground vehicles.

key_facts.fact: Moscow reacted sharply, with the Kremlin calling the missile decision 'fuel on the fire' and saying Russia would respond to possible missile production in Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: kov called it "fuel on the fire," and said Russia... on possible missile... in Ukraine.

stories.headline: FDA clears Jazz's Ziihera for first-line HER2+ stomach cancer with longest survival yet in Phase 3

key_facts.fact: On Aug. 25, 2026, the FDA approved two Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) regimens for first-line treatment of unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma: with Tevimbra (tislelizumab) plus chemotherapy, and with chemotherapy alone.
key_facts.excerpt: DUBLIN, Aug. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Jazz Pharmaceuticals plc (Nasdaq: JAZZ) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved two Ziihera® (zanidatamab-hrii)-containing regimens for the first-line treatment of adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive (HER2+) gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA).

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial, Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy delivered median overall survival of 26.4 months versus 19.2 months for trastuzumab plus chemotherapy — a 28% reduction in the risk of death and the longest median OS reported in a Phase 3 trial in this setting.
key_facts.excerpt: reducing the risk of death by 28% compared with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy and achieving a median OS of 26.4 months versus 19.2 months, representing a greater than seven-month improvement and the longest median OS reported in a Phase 3 trial in HER2+ advanced GEA.

key_facts.fact: Both Ziihera combinations cut the risk of progression or death by 35%, extending median progression-free survival to 12.4 months from 8.1 months.
key_facts.excerpt: reducing the risk of disease progression or death by 35% and extending median PFS to 12.4 months versus 8.1 months with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy.

key_facts.fact: Benefit held regardless of PD-L1 status: in PD-L1-negative tumours (TAP <1%), median OS was 29.7 months with the Tevimbra combination versus 15.8 months in the control arm.
key_facts.excerpt: improvements in OS and PFS were observed across patient subgroups, including patients with PD-L1-negative tumors (TAP <1%), where median OS was 29.7 months with TEVIMBRA plus ZIIHERA and chemotherapy compared with 15.8 months in the control arm.

key_facts.fact: HERIZON-GEA-01 randomised 914 patients across roughly 300 sites in more than 30 countries and was run jointly by Jazz and BeOne Medicines.
key_facts.excerpt: The trial randomized 914 patients from approximately 300 trial sites in more than 30 countries.

key_facts.fact: Zymeworks, which originated zanidatamab, filed an Aug. 25 Form 8-K stating it earned a $250 million milestone from Jazz on the approval, with up to $1.3 billion in further milestones plus 10-20% tiered royalties still possible.
key_facts.excerpt: Zymeworks' August 25, 2026 Form 8-K said the FDA GEA approval earned a $250 million milestone from Jazz. The filing said Zymeworks remains eligible for up to $1.3 billion in additional regulatory and commercial milestones plus tiered royalties of 10% to 20%.

key_facts.fact: The label carries boxed warnings for diarrhoea and embryo-fetal toxicity; in the tislelizumab arm, 59% of 294 patients had serious adverse reactions and 13% permanently discontinued Ziihera.
key_facts.excerpt: high rates of diarrhea, infusion-related reactions and left ventricular dysfunction, and Boxed Warnings for diarrhea and embryo-fetal toxicity... with tislelizumab, 59 percent of 294 patients had serious adverse reactions and 13 percent permanently discontinued Ziihera.

stories.headline: DRC's Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak passes 5,650 cases and 2,700 deaths, still expanding

key_facts.fact: On Aug. 25, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported 5,656 confirmed Bundibugyo virus cases and 2,715 related deaths (data through Aug. 24), an increase of 72 confirmed cases and 35 deaths in a single day.
key_facts.excerpt: On 25 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported a total of 5 656 confirmed cases, including 2 715 related deaths (from data up until 24 August)... This represents an increase of 72 new confirmed cases and 35 deaths since the previous report on 24 August.

key_facts.fact: A total of 792 patients are hospitalised in isolation and 58 of 151 health zones across six provinces are affected; Ituri remains the epicentre with 4,716 cases and 2,119 deaths.
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 792 patients are hospitalised in isolation... Ituri province remains the most affected, with 4 716 cases, including 2 119 deaths... Overall, 58 of 151 health zones are currently affected across the six provinces.

key_facts.fact: WHO said the outbreak has become the DRC's fastest-growing, averaging about 90 confirmed cases a day in its first three months — markedly higher than the 2014-2016 West Africa or 2018-2020 DRC outbreaks over the same period.
key_facts.excerpt: A daily average of around 90 confirmed cases has been recorded in the first three months, markedly higher than the rate observed in the same period during the 2014–2016 West Africa and the 2018–2020 Democratic Republic of the Congo outbreaks.

key_facts.fact: The Bundibugyo species involved has no licensed vaccine or specific treatment; the case fatality ratio stood at 47% as of mid-August, with imported cases already reported in Uganda, France and Germany.
key_facts.excerpt: ongoing transmission, spread to new areas, a high case fatality ratio (47%)... Imported cases have been reported in Uganda, France, and Germany, demonstrating the potential for international spread.

key_facts.fact: WHO's IHR Emergency Committee met a second time on Aug. 18 and issued updated temporary recommendations on Aug. 24, including a new section on social measures, mass gatherings and domestic mobility; the Secretariat rates the risk 'very high' for the DRC.
key_facts.excerpt: On 18 August 2026, the Emergency Committee regarding the epidemic of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo met for the second time... and include a new section on social measures, mass gatherings and domestic mobility.

key_facts.fact: Response capacity has scaled from one testing site to 19 laboratories processing over 3,000 samples a day and from fewer than 10 treatment beds to more than 1,300, with contact follow-up up from 9% to 84%.
key_facts.excerpt: Laboratory capacity has expanded from one testing site to 19 laboratories capable of processing more than 3000 samples a day. Treatment capacity has increased from fewer than 10 beds to more than 1300... contact follow-up has improved from 9% during the first week of the outbreak to 84% as of 18 August.
